title: Development Workflow & Advanced Features 🚀
description: Leverage profiles, watch mode, and overrides to create a smooth developer experience.

slides.title: Service Profiles – Selective Startup 🎯
slides.content:
# Run Only What You Need

Profiles let you group services and start them conditionally.

```yaml
services:
  app:
    image: myapp
    profiles: ["debug"]
```

Start with:
```bash
docker compose --profile debug up
```

Or multiple profiles: `--profile frontend --profile backend`.

> Services without a profile are always started. With a profile, only when that profile is activated.

quizData.question: If a service has `profiles: ["tools"]`, when will it be started by `docker compose up`?
quizData.explanation: Profiled services are opt‑in via the `--profile` flag.

slides.title: Compose Watch – Live Reload 🔄
slides.content:
# Automatic Sync & Rebuild

Compose `watch` (v2.22+) monitors file changes and triggers actions defined in `compose.yaml`:

```yaml
services:
  web:
    build: .
    develop:
      watch:
        - path: ./src
          action: sync
          target: /app/src
        - path: ./package.json
          action: rebuild
```

Start with:
```bash
docker compose up --watch
```

Changes to `src/` are synced instantly; changes to `package.json` trigger a rebuild.

> Great for interpreted languages (Python, Node) without needing bind mounts and custom reload tools.

slides.title: Multiple Compose Files – Override Pattern 🧩
slides.content:
# Base + Environment Specific

Compose automatically reads `compose.override.yaml` if present, merging it on top of `compose.yaml`. You can also specify additional files with `-f`:

```bash
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.prod.yaml up
```

Typical project structure:
- `compose.yaml` – base definition
- `compose.override.yaml` – development overrides (bind mounts, debug ports) – gitignored
- `compose.prod.yaml` – production settings (replicas, logging)

> The later files override/merge with previous ones.

slides.title: Override Example 📦
slides.content:
Base `compose.yaml`:
```yaml
services:
  web:
    image: myapp
    ports:
      - "80:80"
```

Override `compose.override.yaml`:
```yaml
services:
  web:
    build: .
    volumes:
      - .:/app
```

Now `docker compose up` builds locally and mounts code.

quizData.question: What happens when you have both `compose.yaml` and `compose.override.yaml`?

options.text: The two files are merged, with override values taking precedence

quizData.explanation: `compose.override.yaml` is automatically applied on top of the base file. This is great for development tweaks.

slides.title: Development Best Practices 🧑‍💻
slides.content:
# Workflow Tips

- Keep `compose.yaml` version‑controlled with production‑ready defaults.
- Use `compose.override.yaml` for local dev settings (bind mounts, exposed ports, debug flags) and **gitignore** it.
- Use `.env` for environment‑specific values (not secrets!).
- Use profiles for optional tools (adminer, phpMyAdmin, etc.).
- Run `docker compose config` to see the final merged configuration before deployment.
- Integrate `compose up` with your CI to run integration tests against real databases.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## `docker compose config`
This command prints the final, merged configuration without running anything. It’s excellent for debugging and documentation.
